Calling methods on the injected EventStore and TicketStore is orchestration, not persistence logic: the file contains no SQL, connection handling, serialization or storage details. Which layers it may depend on is out of scope here. Rebuilding Event and Ticket objects from the plain records the stores return is a thin mapping step and fits this kind of service. AdmitContextDto has a 'Dto' suffix and an optional requestId field, but it is only an optional type declaration. admit() never reads it, and nothing in the file parses requests, handles HTTP status codes or does any other transport or framework work. So it is a naming signal, not a misplaced responsibility. If it were used for request correlation or tracing, it would be a transport concern that does not belong in the domain.
